subject: Token accounting discrepancy — temporary 429s and billing signal
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Zhao <lina.zhao@acme-retail.com>, ops+infra@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Token accounting discrepancy — temporary 429s and billing signal

Hi Lina / Acme ops team,

I want to let you know about a brief incident that affected a subset of hosted API requests this morning between ~08:40–09:05 UTC. Some clients (including a portion of your traffic) saw elevated 429 responses and anomalous token counts reported in usage.

What happened (summary):
- Between ~08:40 and 09:02 UTC a regression in our token accounting path caused double-counting when prefix caching was combined with streaming responses.
- The double-counting triggered rate-limit enforcement for some customers and produced inflated token usage records for affected requests.
- We pushed a mitigation at 09:02 UTC that disabled the new accounting path and reverted to the stable counter; the rate of 429s dropped to baseline by ~09:05 UTC.

Immediate impact for you:
- You may have seen a short burst of 429s for streaming generation endpoints and an increase in reported token usage for the window above.
- No user data was exposed; this is an accounting and rate-limit regression only.

Next steps we’re taking:
1) Full postmortem and timeline (will share link below).
2) Automated replay and sampling of affected requests to validate counts.
3) Manual review for any customers with material billing delta; we’ll propose credits if warranted.

Attachments: incident-summary-20280620.pdf (short timeline) and token-usage-sample.csv (anonymized sample lines)

We’re sorry for the disruption. I’m personally coordinating remediation — feel free to reply directly if you need immediate help or would like a short call.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Token accounting discrepancy — temporary 429s and billing signal

Thanks Priyom — quick ops note / status: 

- Mitigation timeline: rolled back accounting change at 09:02:18 UTC; canary checks passed by 09:04:55 UTC.
- Root cause (preliminary): an earlier optimization for streaming+prefix-cache introduced a path that incremented both the stream-token counter and the cache-token counter for the same semantic token. That only surfaces on a specific prefix/cache hit pattern (~0.6% of requests at peak).
- Work in flight: open PR to add an idempotency guard to the counter with feature-flag gating; rollback safer default retained for now.
- Customer impact: we logged ~12k affected requests cluster-wide. Rough ballpark for Acme subset: ~1,100 requests (sample in token-usage-sample.csv).

I’ll follow up with a short change that adds end-to-end unit test coverage for combined streaming + cache flows.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
SRE, Infra — Redwood Inference
From: Lina Zhao <lina.zhao@acme-retail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+infra@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:09:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Token accounting discrepancy — temporary 429s and billing signal

Thanks for the heads-up, Priyom. We did see the 429s on a small percentage of streaming generation calls (roughly during 08:45–09:00 UTC).

Couple of questions:
1) Can you confirm whether the inflated token counts will affect our billing for this month? If so, what’s the process and timeline for credits?
2) Any recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance while you roll the fix forward?

If it helps, we can open a short call this afternoon to go over our telemetry.

— Lina
Lina Zhao
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Retail
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Zhao <lina.zhao@acme-retail.com>, ops+infra@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 12:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Token accounting discrepancy — temporary 429s and billing signal

Hi Lina — thanks for confirming. Short answers below and an attached follow-up: incident-summary-20280620.pdf. Full postmortem link: https://internal.redwood.ai/postmortems/2028-06-20-token-accounting

1) Billing impact & credits: We will not charge inflated counts for the affected window. Finance will issue account-level credits for verified deltas. For Acme I’ve flagged the account to the billing team (DEAL-9821). Expect an email with proposed credit by EOD 2028-06-21. If you prefer a faster reconciliation, we can share a CSV of affected request IDs for your audit.

2) Client guidance: We recommend client-side 429 handling with exponential backoff (standard retry with jitter). We do not expect long-term changes to retry logic. The current mitigation is stable; the permanent code fix is under review and will be deployed after test coverage completes.

3) Next steps & timeline:
- 2028-06-20 09:02 UTC — rollback mitigation applied (done)
- 2028-06-20 11:30 UTC — fix merged to main behind feature-flag (rolling canary next 24h)
- 2028-06-21 — billing reconciliation initiated (internal)

If you’d like the meeting, I can set up a 30-minute slot this afternoon to walk telemetry and the credit approach.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we’ll make this right.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
Attachments: incident-summary-20280620.pdf, token-usage-sample.csv
